whyThisShow: This is a Wall of Sound summer night in Jersey City, outdoors at a minor-league baseball stadium two miles from the Statue of Liberty, and the band came in hot. One reviewer called it a "Best of '74 contender" and noted that the first set had "hardly any pauses, the band just wants to go go go". The centerpiece of the first set is a Playing in the Band > Scarlet Begonias > Playing reprise that one listener described as "37 minutes of playing as amazing as the Dead ever got in 1974". The second set closes out with a massive sequence — Sugar Magnolia through He's Gone, Truckin', Spanish Jam, The Other One, Going Down the Road Feeling Bad, and Sunshine Daydream — that one reviewer called "a solid hour of improvisational magic from the heavens". One real caveat: the raw soundboard carries the Wall of Sound's recording limitations, and at least one reviewer flagged "that persistant flat and farty sound to the vocals and that tinny drum sound" — the Dick's Picks 31 release mitigates this somewhat, but it's worth knowing going in.
listenFor: Start with the Eyes of the World — one listener heard "a Slipknot theme buried" in the outro jam and called it "one of the best Eyes out there". In the Playing sandwich, watch for the moment around the 16-minute mark where one reviewer noted "the jam is in a completely different place" before Phil starts "laying down some powerful notes" and it pushes into exploratory territory. In the second set, don't skip past the Spanish Jam — one reviewer specifically flagged the "well developed Spanish Jam" as a highlight not to miss. Also worth noting: Bobby flubs the Truckin' lyrics and "literally says 'Whoops!' into the microphone before recovering". And if you want to hear what the Wall of Sound actually sounded like from inside the room, at least one reviewer recommends cross-referencing the audience recording alongside the soundboard.
context: August 6, 1974 fell between the two-night Philly run (August 4–5) and the band's departure for the legendary Alexandra Palace shows in England that September. The recording here is a soundboard (identifier: gd74-08-06.sbd.deadlists.1463.sbeok.shnf), and portions of the show were released officially on Dick's Picks Vol. 31, though that release was not complete. One reviewer noted the show "was a well-traded show long before a few lesser parts were released on Dick's Picks #31" and that "because Dick's 31 wasn't complete, it misses the best stuff and loses the sense of the purposeful development of the show". This was also one of the last shows before Mickey Hart rejoined the band, with one reviewer observing that Billy's "propulsion and extra fills" may be part of what drives the energy.
funFact: Bobby stopped the show mid-set to police the crowd, and his instruction — "Don't climb on the fence, idiot" — caught on tape as what one reviewer called "a humorous bit of advice to the fans that tried to scale the barbed wire topped barrier in front of the stage".
headline: Wall of Sound, Jersey City, August '74 — all of it.
